In terms of priorities, education and marketing are huge. Though, there needs to be some recognition that Edgeware is broadly targeting two different groups of people that sometimes overlap: devs and other users.

If we're looking to expand adoption, it needs to be clear to people who are not devs but who might be interested in the project what they can do with Edgeware. So, if that's participating in governance and using dapps that build on Edgeware, that needs to be communicated much differently than you would communicate to devs. It should probably also happen on the website first (but also in other mediums), which I understand is part of what's currently happening. But frankly, nobody in this space is doing a great job of helping to communicate concepts in a way that is understandable to non-technical people. I think this is a key area where Edgeware could/will be different. (This is in addition to the marketing/education happening targeting devs. It's obviously critical to speak to both groups.)

Also, the governance structure needs to be much clearer. Honestly, I've been following the project for a while and still don't 100% understand how everything fits together. Would be great to see proposals in plain language, or even a Schoolhouse Rock type explanation for understanding how the DAO system works for non-tech people who want to learn but feel like the learning curve is insurmountable.

Awesome Rich, thank you for the links. This resonates with me:

"Right now we're arguing about the components of a company (smart contracts included) - without anyone caring what the company does, who runs it what their story is or what they hope to achieve." 

It always amazes me how humbling this work is; so many pieces to the coordination puzzle.

Comforting to see how thoughtful and deliberate we are.

> quite a few Q3/Q4 theses on DAOs (and I think I saw DAOs of DAOs ??).

[@Dres](/edgeware/account/5DyNL5VAhncUJ4nSyMKPTbQUzfJ3wCxp6uBaWUvoh2aBkaec) Decentralised organisations subsume all the the other pieces of the stack into a human organisation, and it will be this organisation that becomes relatable. 

Right now we're kind of arguing about the components of a company (smart contracts included) - without anyone caring what the company does, who runs it what their story is or what they hope to achieve.

Edgeware is already a DAO of DAOs, just in a very primitive fashion. Substrate (and Cosmos SDK) enables layer 1 protocol DAOs with community treasuries are going to change the whole landscape in the next couple of years - it's just hard to see over the horizon just now. 

See [this post](https://github.com/monsieurbulb/forksintheroad/blob/master/Decred_forks_in_the_road.md) on Decred (the OG layer 1  protocol DAO), very relevant to Edgeware and any other chain with the same design.

All Substrate chains are going to have to figure out this DAO / DAO of DAOs structure - its waaaay harder than just tech, because it's also about people. 

[DAO of DAOs link here ](https://www.notboring.co/p/the-dao-of-daos)- but it misses the fundamental insight that layer 2 DAO's (those built on ETH) are all profit driven and this will ensure a focus on token price above proposals that have a longer timeline or are not immediately commercial. This will imo lead to a very short term mindset in ETH DAOs, especially where creators are concerned. It adds money into an already dysfunctional attention game that influencers peddle.

** we have a lot of rad things to talk about when the time comes: Substrate, Interoperability, DAOs, Derivatives (dTrade), Swaps. We are also getting more signal from legacy world that they're joining crypto. Paul Tudor Jones today allocating 5% of his net worth to BTC (reiterting), Mark Cuban w a thoughtful note on defi and some assets - and quite a few Q3/Q4 theses on DAOs (and I think I saw DAOs of DAOs ??).

We have an exciting window of opportunity.

Hi [@Thom Ivy](/edgeware/account/jKauGVPCQkteGTDKuuNwhYhMBrj5QuytgybEC4A5cS4Bki5) - apologies as I am just seeing this now. What I mean by overhang is like an artificial ceiling - a barrier to go higher as a trading/price/story/narrative/momentum metaphor. As an example, I think a large buyer of any asset might be reticent or wary knowing there are many holders (supply) in the hands of addresses that might be true sellers when they are able.

These addresses have not had the 'freedom' to get out of their position, a position that has been held most likely for a few years. My guess is these addresses are natural sellers for all sorts of healthy reasons. IMO, we want to give these addresses **as soon as possible** the ability to get out. So, the true believers, the ones who want to be here can be the 'strong hands'. 

I think it's important bc once we get momentum, we do not want to have these 'overhangs' but just blue skies = price discovery.

Right now part of our supply is held hostage. We need to unlock this so when our strory does get the momentum and praise it deserves, we're not like, "awesome, oh f^%$, another wave of selling coming". Because I think it will.

Edit: I also think this makes our OTC job more difficult - if this is something we are focusing on. A potential size holder probably would not take full size through EDG OTC with poss more of a supply dump coming.

*Caveat: I might not fully understand the lockdrop scenario (Binance, etc) and the supply that needs to change hands...If so, mega apologies.
[@Dres](/edgeware/account/5DyNL5VAhncUJ4nSyMKPTbQUzfJ3wCxp6uBaWUvoh2aBkaec)  Can you clarify what you mean by overhang?

*to add: and we make sure our current core dev Team is good-to-go. 

Is critical that they're motivated.

I would like to see Edgeware focus on:

- Hiring more core devs - aggressively build out in this cycle, especially if we in 'bear' for a bit.
- Remove Lockdrop Distribution overhang. I think this supply is hurting us and the sooner we remove it, the better we are. We should no longer game exchanges - I think buyers in size who do their work will be less motivated to accumulate until this occurs. I think this can benefit us at current levels.

If we can solve liquidity issues then at least we can begin a path to paying developers in EDG. We will need to identify a clear path of demand for the platform. Here are things I've always liked thinking of:

# Bridges
- Experiment with parity-common-bridges and start setting up bridges with any parachains that will be open to it.
- Bridge to other large ecosystems that should have easy compatibility: Cosmos, Celo, NEAR. A single person to take charge on these items. It would amount to 2-3 core devs.
- IBC pallet exists
- Solidity GRANDPA light client is only thing stopping EVM bridges and chains which are more relaxed on precompile support may be good targets (not Ethereum but Celo, Harmony, Avalanche)
- NEAR should be able to support a bridge since they support Rust contracts.


# Oracles
- Experiment with web oracles like MINA is.


# Education
- Edgeware should start hosting more hackathons for Ink! / pallet development
- We should engage Rust deveopment/education shops and partner where possible
- We should bring on a developer education lead who can guide devs through small projects.


# Tech
- Integrate zksync like Plasm has. This could be a good early thing for early zk engineers to have more testing grounds outside of a production zksync against Ethereum.

## Mission Critical Priorities

1. Liquidity crunch, market making, OTC and Exchange listings. 
2. These are urgent to bootstrapping Edgeware.
3. Demand creation pursuant to 1 - improving marketing, website, and investor perception, reconnecting with DOT marketing venues.
4. Recruiting a core technical contributor and coordinator. 
5. Parachain Strategy, including setting a clear plan and timeline for research of alternatives, and resolving any use cases for Hedgeware or a community owned canarynet. 
6. Bridging from ETH to improve assets on EDG. 
7. Driving staking up as a matter of improving markets and network security. Including community validators, testnet validation, and treasury-as-validator staking.
8. Asset management: After bridging to ETH, working to give the treasury a stablecoin supply. 



## High Priorities

- Onboarding ecosystem partners.
- Finalizing Ledger integration.
- Solving EVM and improving developer experience with grants, bounties, and better co-support.
have done [@raymondz](/straightedge/account/str186wygrqrgykzcr5s0alajur0p2ddc7qe8fxdkz) - sorry running on too much coffee today.

My two cents on this topic:

- **Hedging treasuries funds**(stable coins, decred, or any other asset not tight to the BTC fluctuation). The amount of hedged funds can be a separated topic in itself. It can be done via OTC, till hedge is completed. I think it's very important thing to do because we all know that $EDG price goes up/down along side the overall crypto market. It would take stress off from the Agency and the people working/contributing to the chain.
- **Hiring new core devs**. As Drew is about to leave the Edgeware, we really need to address this. As RUST devs are in the high demand, maybe we could hire C++ dev. From what I've read RUST and C++ are quite similar, but I'm not an expert in any of these languages, so might be missing some insight. 
- **Ledger integration**, this comes along side the core devs we have contributing to the project.
- **Exchanges**. This topic been already discussed and seems to be moving forward, although I would not attribute the price of $EDG to the listing on new exchanges. Look at Bittrex listing. In the short term/hype it might have some effect, but in the long run the investors should see the value of the community, the chain and the ability to participate in it.
- **Marketing**, was also recently discussed. We should find the well known public figures who sees the potential, future vision of the Edgeware and are genuinely in to seeing it succeed.
- **Lockdrop distribution,** which is still pending. I know that some people are afraid of this happening and potential dump of $EDG, but I think that's very important and should be pursued. Is there something that can be done from our end?
@Rich can you sum up your views in a shorter form - a few sentences or bullet points? Just to make it more accessible for everyone.

**What should Edgeware be focused on?**

We cannot do everything, we have limited resources and limited funding compared to other projects and we will move slower since we are so community oriented.

One thing that people should realise is that there are a range of factors that **Edgeware is a slow burn.**

- We cannot become successful overnight 
- Many benefits are not immediately obvious and will play out over time.
- To optimise for short term decisions destroys the foundations on which a community is built.


Therefore everything we fund should be a **high leverage decision,** tightly aligned to a core strategy, evolving governance, investment thesis and community focus.

- **By High leverage I mean **things that give us 10x / 100x benefits over other projects, see:
- [Edgeware's Key Differentiators and Benefits](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1133-defining-edgewares-key-differentiators-benefits)
- [On The Edge: A Collective Vision for the future of Edgeware](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1176-out-on-the-edge-a-collective-vision-for-the-future-of-edgeware)


Out strategy should be focused on things that are:
- Novel
- Inexpensive
- Differentiated
- Scaleable
- **High leverage areas that are not yet competed out.**
- Collectively bring alive just why Edgeware is different.
- The win is the collective endeavours and cross-collective integration.


**In simple terms - we are initially focusing on building bridges between people, not chains.  **

This strategy should build on core project differentiators - a vertically integrated ‘Appchain’ with a one line pitch.

We will get nowhere being generic in the first instance.

What is Edgeware's story? Back to the original discussion where[ @dillon](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/account/iCLdev9eJBSaUSD1qnbq1roqcV6jZmfLpbLJjTdmUocixcY) suggested making Edgeware 'a meme'.

By that he means how can we distill Edgeware's proposition and story into a super simple and evocative story.
We build through the stack first:

- Smart contracts (base layer / undifferentiated / easy to copy / no moat)
- Community funding / Edgeware as Incubator
- Governance of said funds and teams 
- Network of DAOs
- Web3 media


This is also our Trojan Horse for:

- Chain Factory
- Relay chain
- Everything else… 


What every blockchain community is trying to build is a ‘publishing network’ on a sovereign financial and organisational stack, they just haven’t realised it yet. Edgeware is no different. 

- **We are building a multichain media network, on sovereign organisational and financial systems from the inside out.**


We orient around a single simple but credible proposition that can cut through and sell.

- **“MTV for the crypto generation” or similar.**


Without any tech innovation, without parachains, without defi, with the basic building blocks we have today - multisig, governance, community, smart contracts we can build a world famous publishing network in 24 months. 

If we do, people can stop worrying about EDG price, because we will have one of the most famous crypto-currencies in the world. 

I’m not overly concerned about any of the below - they will happen, if it takes a few more weeks or months that is not a big deal - we're wasting time obsessing over stuff that isn't high leverage. 

In the end racing to get a ‘parachain’ is not a dealbreaker in the above. 

This is a strategy that plays to our strengths - it is contrarian, but that's what we need.

Responding to[ @DostoPat](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/account/mZCf9EK1RYqApCt4o4gZhZffTnPUNQ8x6RJPs1u1HoQmU2L):

> We should stop funding proposals which don't benefit either Edgeware's technical infrastructure or bring a clear direct benefit to Edgeware.

This requires a clear strategic rationale for how we qualify ‘direct benefit’. 

The Web3 media strategy ties things together that will soon make much more sense. 

Every time we fund a project such as Commonwealth.im, Webb, Zien, MoCDA or New-Futures is that we are recruiting technical talent, they just happen to have that talent wrapped in a Web3 media project.

In this way we don't recruit 'core devs' who solely look inwards and do not have any intention to their design or vision in their work.

- **Webb, how do we make ZKsnarks useful / understandable?**
- Build anonymous creator collectives.


- **Commonwealth - how do we drive use of governance systems?**
- Commonwealth is a publishing system... 
- Onboard creator networks


- **Common protocol - how do we drive use of kickstarter**
- Target creators.


- **DTrade - decentralised options trading? **
- Integrating this thinking into a 'creator first' model
- Speculate on the careers of artists and musicians

# mid-term goals

As mid-term goal we should really prepare for the parachain auction and aim for the first spot.
We could dedicate 50% of the treasury to this in order to buy Dot. While acquiring Dot, this Dot can be stake to either buy more Dot or rebuy EDG.
In order to liquidate EDG for Dot, we could do something similar what EOS has done in its 1 year ICO.
Every 2 days a pool of EDG is distributed. People can qualify by sending Dot to an address and based on their Dot fraction of sent DOT they get the fraction EDG in this distribution round. For EOS this always had lead to last moment sending of ETH, to a large accumulation of ETH in the end and thus to a higher amount of ETH collected, compared to theoretically amount based on the ticker price. 
This also brought massive awareness to EOS.

This of course would need a referendum and either a person dedicated to liquidating EDG for DOT or with the EOS approach or something similar is taken, a technical person for the smart contracts and the data processing/visualisation

# long-term goals

Edgeware as relay chain. This requires the recruitment of technical people and a clear technical outline.

body: I agree with Raymondz, all 4 main points of focus are relevant. Just wanted to highlight "a parachain bonding". As I remember in the past there were opinions that maybe we shouldn't aim for the 1st parachain auction but rather wait for a while and acquire spot later when it will be cheaper. In my opinion this could lead Edgeware to lose momentum and indeed we should try to get parachain as soon as possible.

I missed the call, but I agree with the above points and to expand on each point, my thoughts:

- The core development priorities should fall into the strategic objectives of Edgeware. What are those? Imo,
- Interoperability: Aim to connect to the top 20 Substrate chains. 
- And aim to build the next new substrate chains, bond with them and have a voting stake.
- Given Edgeware's experience as a substrate chain, it can enable other new chains as a launchpad, and be a center of a web of chains through bonding and bridging. 
- Making the very best experience for users through making the wallet even better than the raw features Polkadot JS apps offer to users. 
- Be a beacon in the Substrate community. The Substrate technical community is still surprisingly small, this will change and people need to think of Edgeware after they think of Polkadot and Kusama.  
- Controversial idea: Consider removing the evm-pallet. Consider removing smart contracts. This splits focus from bonding with other chains.
- Encourage pallet development and fund it. 
- Offer match funding from parity projects, and onboard some parity funded projects into Edgeware as an incubator. 
- Education.
- Create an Edgeware-node-template, which has custom build scripts and makes it easier to set up a working chain.
